How to regression-test prompts when switching LLM models

Switching model or editing a prompt changes outputs in ways unit tests do not see. Save before and after outputs, then run the diff tool over them.

Why do prompts break when I change models?

Models differ in how closely they follow format instructions, how readily they refuse, how long they write and where they stop. A prompt tuned against one model can start returning prose around your JSON, drop a field, or end mid-sentence on another, and none of that shows up in a unit test of the surrounding code.

What should my baseline be?

Run your real prompts over a fixed set of inputs on the current model, and save each result with a stable id as JSONL. Keep 20 to 100 cases that cover your hardest formats. Re-run the same inputs on the candidate model or prompt and save those the same way, then compare the two files.

How do I fail a pull request on a regression?

Run the CLI in your workflow after the candidate run and let its exit code decide: node cli.mjs diff baseline.jsonl candidate.jsonl --max-regressions 0. Exit 1 means regressions exceeded the limit; use --fail-on warn to be stricter.

What does a clean result not tell me?

That the candidate is as good. These are deterministic text checks. They catch format and contract breaks cheaply, and they leave factual accuracy, tone and safety to your own evaluation and review.

A minimal CI step

- run: node cli.mjs diff baseline.jsonl candidate.jsonl --max-regressions 0

Did the new model or prompt break your outputs?

Paste your saved outputs from before and after a model swap or prompt edit (one JSON object per line with an id and an output). Get a per-case list of what broke: invalid JSON, lost keys, new refusals, truncation, lost numbers, lost formatting.

Gate it in CI

node cli.mjs diff baseline.jsonl candidate.jsonl
node cli.mjs diff baseline.jsonl candidate.jsonl --max-regressions 2 --fail-on warn
node cli.mjs diff baseline.jsonl candidate.jsonl --json

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. Exit 1 when regressions exceed the limit. More: How to regression-test prompts when switching LLM models.

Common questions

Does this call any model or API?

No. It compares two files of outputs you already saved. It makes no network call, needs no API key and never sees your prompts unless you put them in the output text.

What does it actually check?

Per case id: empty or missing output, JSON that stopped parsing or lost keys or changed a value's type, new refusal or apology wording, unclosed code fences, large length changes, numbers that disappeared, lost lists, headings or code blocks, truncation, and low word overlap. Errors are likely to break a consumer; warnings deserve a human look.

Is this a quality score for a model?

No. It is a tripwire for changes, not a judge of which output is better. A flagged case can be an improvement and a clean case can still be worse; read the flagged ones and keep your own evaluation for quality.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The page works in your browser and sends nothing. The CLI reads local files only.
